moonlighter-2-dungeon-extraction-guide.title: Moonlighter 2 Dungeon Extraction Guide: When to Turn Back
moonlighter-2-dungeon-extraction-guide.description: When to leave a Moonlighter 2 dungeon, how to protect relics, and how to make a repeatable extraction decision after version 1.0.
moonlighter-2-dungeon-extraction-guide.intro: The safest Moonlighter 2 dungeon route is not always the deepest one. Extraction is the bridge between a successful fight and a shop inventory, so the decision should weigh the haul already in your backpack, remaining healing, the next route choice, and what failure would cost you. This version 1.0 field guide turns that decision into a repeatable check. It does not claim a magic room count or one health threshold that fits every build; instead, it helps you identify when another room has a purpose and when returning is the stronger play.

sections.heading: Set a run objective before entering
paragraphs: A useful run starts with a reason to go out. Pick one primary goal: gather a kind of relic, replenish shop stock, make progress toward a named upgrade, learn a route, or practice a fight. If several goals compete, rank them. A route that serves a specific purpose gives you a better return decision than a vague plan to “go deeper.” It also helps you tell the difference between a run that failed and a run that completed its objective early.

Keep that objective small enough to evaluate at a doorway. “Find one material I need for the next town improvement” is actionable. “Get rich” does not tell you when the risk stops being worthwhile. The public release description establishes the repeating dungeon-to-shop-to-village loop, so a successful trip can be measured by what it enables after you return, not only by how many rooms you crossed.

Before leaving, note the current build, your equipment or ability choice, and what counts as success for this trip. You do not need a full spreadsheet for every run. A short target helps you avoid changing your purpose halfway through just because another room might contain more loot. For a detailed item and pricing record, pair this page with the relic and loot guide and dungeon guide.

sections.heading: Check the haul before adding more risk
paragraphs: At each transition, pause long enough to see what is already secured. Does the backpack contain the item or category you came for? Is there a material you can convert into an upgrade? Is the bag now awkward enough that another find could force a costly rearrangement? These questions put current value in front of imagined future value. You cannot sell a room you have not reached, but you can protect the haul you already collected by ending the run.

The decision is not simply “full bag means leave.” Backpack pressure is one input, and the puzzle may still have a safe arrangement. If there is room and the next area serves your objective, continuing may be reasonable. If moving one new item would make the existing set harder to carry, the next pickup has a cost even before you see it. Record the trade you are accepting rather than assuming every open slot is free capacity.

Use the customer and price loop after extraction to learn whether the haul had practical value. Until you test an item, its exact shop price is unknown. Do not risk a finished objective for an assumed number that the game has not shown you. Once back in Tresna, turn the run into evidence: what sold, what was kept, what funded a town plan, and which item should be the target next time.

sections.heading: Use a doorway decision checklist
paragraphs: Before opening the next door, ask four questions. First, can your current equipment and remaining healing handle a likely fight? Second, do you understand the route back or the extraction option available in this part of the run? Third, would losing this particular haul harm the next shop or village step? Fourth, is the next room connected to the goal you set before leaving? A “no” is not automatically a command to turn around, but it tells you where the risk sits.

If your survival answer is uncertain and the haul matters, returning is usually the rational choice. If the route is known, the inventory is stable, and the next encounter is part of the objective, continuing can be a deliberate test. Avoid using a rigid count such as “always leave after three rooms”; room difficulty and the value of your current bag can change. A fixed threshold sounds easy to remember but hides the choices that actually determine the outcome.

Make one decision at a time. You do not have to choose between ending the entire session and clearing every branch. Extract, sell or store the result, spend what you need, and start another attempt with updated information. Repeated controlled trips often teach more than a single overextended run whose final loss obscures where the risk began.

sections.heading: Price the cost of a failed run honestly
paragraphs: Moonlighter’s released store information warns that dungeon decisions and returning with loot are part of the game’s central loop, but public material does not give a universal formula for every death, item loss, or recovery case. Check the wording and behavior in your current build. If a failure removes, rearranges, or otherwise changes inventory, record exactly what you saw and do not generalize one incident into a hidden rule for every mode.

A practical comparison includes the time and resources already spent, the items currently in the backpack, the next shop or upgrade goal, and the likely cost of having to repeat the route. A small haul can still be worth extracting if it answers a route question. A valuable haul can justify a cautious extra room if you have a clear exit. Neither case has a universal gold threshold because players’ plans and builds differ.

On a new or experimental file, reduce the amount of progress at risk until you understand its rules. The page on difficulty and death collects the release language and the things it does not specify. For Hardcore, use the separate Hardcore Mode guide and treat its consequences as a different risk profile. Do not use an ordinary run’s assumptions to make a permanent-save decision.

sections.heading: Treat healing as a budget, not a dare
paragraphs: Healing left in reserve is not proof that you should continue until it is gone. It is insurance against a difficult encounter, a mistake, or an unfamiliar route. If you spend most of it before you reach the branch you came to explore, the value of continuing has fallen even when your health bar is not yet empty. Pause at safe transitions and judge the resource you will have after the next likely fight, not just the current display.

When learning a boss or elite encounter, separate practice from haul protection. A run carrying a carefully assembled shop stock may be the wrong time to test an unknown pattern. If the goal is learning, consider arriving with less progress to lose and record the attack or event that forced you to spend healing. Your future self can use the observation without risking the same valuable bag again.

Avoid claiming that a particular weapon or armor setup guarantees safe extraction unless you tested it against the encounter and build in question. Equipment changes your options, but the public version 1.0 materials do not provide a complete damage table or universal boss route. Cross-reference the weapons page and best armor guide for the confirmed gear categories, then make encounter-specific conclusions from repeatable play.

sections.heading: Route knowledge changes the answer
paragraphs: An unfamiliar branch carries information risk in addition to combat risk. You may not know its layout, the safest way back, or whether an exit is available where you expect it. On an exploratory trip, consider leaving earlier with a modest haul and a useful map note. That note can make a later attempt safer, even though the first run did not reach the deepest area.

Record a branch in a way you can act on: where you chose it, what you found, whether a fight consumed resources, and what landmark or connection helped you orient. Do not invent coordinates or guaranteed room contents. If the branch changes between attempts, preserve both outcomes and label them by version or run. The purpose is to improve your next choice, not to pretend a changing dungeon is a fixed map.

Once you know the route, the same branch may become an efficient way to pursue a goal. You can then compare the added haul with the healing, time, and backpack rearrangement it requires. Route knowledge does not make the area harmless; it makes the uncertainty more manageable. Reassess whenever a patch or equipment change might have altered the conditions you previously learned.

sections.heading: Extract, then turn the return into progress
paragraphs: A return trip is only half of the decision. Back in Tresna, sort the haul into items to sell, materials to keep, and anything reserved for an upgrade. Record sale prices and customer reactions separately from estimates. If an upgrade changes your next trip, note what it cost and what new option it added. This conversion from inventory to information and village progress is why an early exit can still be a successful run.

Do not spend everything automatically. First compare the sale result with your stated objective. If you came back for a specific crafting or town need, keep what advances it. If the goal was shop inventory, record what sold and what remains. The shop guide explains the business side, while the postgame guide covers the different goals after the main story.

Then choose the next outing based on the result. A run that reveals an item’s placement problem may call for a different backpack plan. A route that drained healing may need better equipment or a different branch. An item with an unknown response may call for a controlled pricing test. Each completed return should make a later decision better informed.

sections.heading: Endless Vault uses a separate success condition
paragraphs: After the main story, the Infinite Endless Vault introduces one-run gold thresholds. The published version 1.0 description says progress for a threshold resets when a run falls short, which changes how you define a useful exit. Check the current target shown by the game and plan around that displayed requirement. Do not borrow a normal exploration rule when the Vault asks for a specific amount in one run.

No universal threshold number, depth, or guaranteed reward schedule is published in the available launch material. Track the target shown in your build, the amount collected, and whether the run met it. If you fall short, note which decision caused the gap: an early exit, a price assumption, or a route that consumed resources. Because this is a run-based goal, preserving an old threshold total is not the same thing as finishing the current attempt.

For the detailed postgame rules, see the Infinite Endless Vault guide and rewards overview. This article’s general check still helps, but the correct point to extract must be evaluated against the live target displayed for that attempt.

sections.heading: A short field log after each run
paragraphs: Write down the build, objective, area or branch, the point where you considered turning back, the state of your haul and healing, the decision you made, and the outcome. Add one sentence about what you would do differently. This is enough to build a practical route history without inventing exact room limits or prices. If the result contradicts an older entry, preserve both and explain the changed condition. Over time you will recognize which objectives justify another door and which ones are better served by a safe return.

sections.heading: A reliable rule for the next door
paragraphs: Continue only when the next step has a clear purpose and your current run can afford its risk. Extract when the goal is already met, the bag is valuable to your plan, your ability to recover is shrinking, or the route has become too uncertain to justify. This is not a promise that every cautious run will succeed; it is a decision process you can apply, review, and improve in the released game.

moonlighter-2-best-armor.title: Moonlighter 2 Best Armor
moonlighter-2-best-armor.description: Moonlighter 2 armor is bought in Tresna after you sell the bag. There is no official armor tier list with damage numbers.
moonlighter-2-best-armor.intro: Choose armor by the effect shown on your current build and the encounter that is giving you trouble. This guide compares documented set roles with a practical method for deciding whether an equipment purchase improves your next attempt.

sections.heading: Why there is no honest S-tier yet
paragraphs: Version 1.0, out of Early Access on September 2, 2026, names four Endless Weapon Aspects and describes their specials. It does not do the same for armor. The store page says village investment unlocks better weapons, armor, and upgrades. That is a category, not a ranking. A page that labels an unnamed chestplate S-tier is inventing the number the launch post refused to print.

Hotfix 1 on September 10 did name one armor bug. Players could become invincible in boss fights after equipping the Scarabastion. That line is a fix, not a recommendation. An unusually easy encounter alone does not establish that your save triggered the reported bug. Update, unequip it, and fight the boss again before you call that piece the best armor in the game. Invincibility that a patch removed is not a build.

sections.heading: Buy armor the way you buy a potion
paragraphs: Separate the risk attached to carried relics from the effect of equipped armor. Read the penalty description on your current difficulty before starting a valuable run, particularly on Hardcore. Then inspect the armor effect in the equipment screen and choose one problem to address: an opening hit, an unsafe recovery, or a build interaction. Do not assume that owning armor protects every kind of progress. A useful purchase is one you can explain in terms of the encounter you are preparing for and the resources you still need afterward.

After returning to Tresna, inspect the resources available for equipment and the items you still want to sell. Decide whether the last attempt failed because of damage taken or because of movement and timing. Armor is easier to evaluate when you keep the weapon and route familiar. If you change both at once, an easier fight cannot be attributed confidently to either purchase. Preserve enough resources for the rest of your preparation rather than spending every available coin on a set whose effect you have not learned.

Shop Level 5, named in the September 2 post, adds one more Bloblet slot and one more cosmetic placement slot. Those are shop slots, not armor stats. Do not skip a piece of armor you die without in order to decorate a floor you have not funded. Cosmetics are confirmed. They are not mitigation.
bullets: Buy the potion first if you are still dying
Empty the bag before the next door
Weapons have named specials. Armor does not.

sections.heading: What to write down when you do test a piece
paragraphs: If you equip something and the next elite takes fewer hits to put you down, write the item name in the game's words, the dungeon, and the patch. That note is a personal log. It is not a tier list until a second run on the same piece agrees. Scarabastion taught the opposite lesson: a piece can lie until the hotfix. Retest any "best armor" claim from the first week of September on Hotfix 1 or newer.

The gun is not an armor slot and not a fifth melee class. Four melee classes are named: Short Swords, Large Swords, Spears, and Gauntlets. The gun rides alongside. Do not put the gun on an armor ranking because a search asked for best gun. That search wants a weapon page. This page is the town purchase that stays when the bag does not.

sections.heading: A purchase you can defend
paragraphs: Update to Hotfix 1. For repeated PC crashes, use the controlled graphics-API comparison in the troubleshooting guide. Confirm Scarabastion is not granting a boss-fight invincibility the patch said it removed. Sell the bag. Buy the armor you died wishing you had. Leave the unnamed S-tier to a later patch that actually prints defense numbers.

Before buying an upgrade, compare its price with your available balance and the next activity you intend to attempt. Keep the old setup identifiable so you can compare it with the replacement. On a short familiar route, note the same enemy, the armor effect as displayed, whether its trigger occurred and whether you could use the resulting opening. One successful encounter is a reason to keep testing, rather than proof of a universal best item. If a benefit depends on Spark perks, evaluate it with the perks actually equipped instead of judging the item from its name.

sections.heading: Moonlighter 2 Nimbus Regalia — Armor Set Guide
paragraphs: Nimbus Regalia is a armor set in Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault, added in Greed & Glory (Mar 2026). The set combines an initial shield with an offensive opportunity after the shield breaks. Use the current description for its amount and duration; an unfamiliar attack is a poor way to test whether the follow-up is useful.

sections.heading: Special effect
paragraphs: The set is described around a shield and a damage opportunity when that shield breaks. Use the current equipment description to check the trigger and duration, then ask whether you can attack safely during that opening. Do not deliberately absorb an unfamiliar boss attack solely to activate an offensive effect.
bullets: Class: Armor Set.
Class mechanic: Andrei forges armor as well as weapons. Armor sets change how you survive a run rather than how you swing.
Added: Greed & Glory (Mar 2026).

sections.heading: How to get
paragraphs: Quest for the crafting recipe, which appears once you reach the second Aeolia floor.

sections.heading: Best use
paragraphs: A defensive set with an offensive payoff: the free Shield absorbs one opener, and the break window rewards trading it for a damage burst.

sections.heading: Moonlighter 2 Endless Void Armour — Armor Set Guide
paragraphs: Endless Void Armour is a armor set in Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault, added in 1.0 (Sep 2026). Increased base critical hit chance, plus additional critical damage for every Spark perk equipped.

sections.heading: Special effect
paragraphs: Increased base critical hit chance, plus additional critical damage for every Spark perk equipped.
bullets: Class: Armor Set.
Class mechanic: Andrei forges armor as well as weapons. Armor sets change how you survive a run rather than how you swing.
Added: 1.0 (Sep 2026).

sections.heading: How to get
paragraphs: Version 1.0, forged by the Golden Guild.

sections.heading: Best use
paragraphs: The crit set for Spark builds. The more Spark perks you run, the more critical damage it adds, so stack Spark on the perk tree.

moonlighter-2-endless-vault-rewards.title: Moonlighter 2 Endless Vault Rewards
moonlighter-2-endless-vault-rewards.description: Version 1.0 names Endless Vault rewards as a gold-target ladder. The gold numbers themselves were not published.
moonlighter-2-endless-vault-rewards.intro: The Infinite Endless Vault is the version 1.0 postgame, unlocked after the main story. Each threshold has to be cleared in a single run. Falling short of the required gold resets progress on that threshold. The September 2 post names the ladder. It does not print the gold targets.

sections.heading: What is confirmed about the rewards
paragraphs: The launch post describes the Vault as a gold-target ladder past the story ending. You clear a threshold in one run. If the gold is short, that threshold's progress resets. That is the reward structure: the next step exists only if this run paid for it. It is not a chest list with published item names and drop rates.

The same post names Endless Vault cosmetics, new vendors, and Codex pages for enemies, characters, perks, and furniture. Cosmetics and Codex entries are the reward categories that were actually written down. A guide that fills the missing gold numbers with forum guesses is not more useful than the sentence the studio printed. Write "unpublished" in the gold column until you have recorded a run yourself, with the patch version next to it.

Four Endless Weapon Aspects shipped in the same build: Endless Short Sword, Endless Great Sword, Endless Spear, and Endless Gauntlets. They are weapon specials, not Vault gold targets. Do not put them in the reward table as if the Vault drops them at a named floor. The aspects have described specials. The Vault has a described reset rule. Keep the two pages separate.

sections.heading: How a failed threshold actually feels
paragraphs: The threshold reset described in the launch announcement concerns progress toward that challenge. It should not be expanded into a complete inventory-retention guarantee. Before an attempt, inspect the chosen difficulty and distinguish failure to meet a target from character death. Keep a record of the balance and relevant unlocks before entering, then compare the result screen with the hub state afterward. This makes it possible to identify what changed without assuming that every reward, purchase or carried item follows the same rule.

Hardcore is a different reset. Version 1.0 describes it as a progress loss, a separate campaign, not a relic-quality tax. Do not practice Vault thresholds on a Hardcore file. Practice them on the file that keeps the town. Easy, Normal, and Hard still halve backpack quality on a normal death. Expert still deletes the relics. The Vault adds a gold reset on top of whatever difficulty you already picked. Read both penalties before you open the door.

Hotfix 1 did not publish the gold targets either. It fixed a Kalina hole, a Scarabastion invincibility bug, Hazy Jane eating input, and a pile of enemy and weapon bugs. If a Vault run dies to a crash, switch DirectX 11 and 12 before you blame the gold rule. A crash is not a short threshold. A short threshold is a rule you can plan for once the game stays open.
bullets: The Vault ladder in more detail
Sell before you wager the next threshold
What September 2 actually named

sections.heading: A reward table you are allowed to keep
paragraphs: Use three columns: threshold you attempted, gold you actually extracted, and whether the game advanced you. Leave a fourth column blank for the required gold until the UI shows it on your build. That fourth number is yours to copy down. It is not a number this page can invent for every patch.

Cosmetics and Codex pages are the named extras. If a vendor in the postgame sells a Vault cosmetic, write the price the vendor shows. Steam's store description still says you set shop prices for relics. It does not say the Vault vendors use the same system. Read the vendor. Do not apply the shop minigame to a postgame NPC without looking.

Treat a reward record as a description of one completed challenge. Include the threshold label, the target shown before entry, the result shown after the attempt and any newly accessible service or cosmetic. If you inspect a vendor afterward, distinguish an item that became available from an item you actually received. Availability, purchase and possession are different states. When an entry is incomplete, record the missing field explicitly rather than filling it from a different player’s video. Before committing currency, inspect the current description and ask whether the reward supports your next goal or is a collectible you can postpone. A clear result log is useful even when the attempt falls short, because it identifies whether the next change should be route planning, survival or a misunderstanding of the target.

sections.heading: Inspect the result screen
paragraphs: Record the reward shown after your own successful clear before spending it. A useful note includes the challenge and the save state, so a later comparison does not mix an earlier progression reward with a repeat completion.

moonlighter-2-bag-before-the-door.title: Empty the Moonlighter 2 Bag Before the Next Door
moonlighter-2-bag-before-the-door.description: A Moonlighter 2 death still taxes the backpack. Sell in Tresna before the next elite if the relics are the prize.
moonlighter-2-bag-before-the-door.intro: Before entering another dungeon, inspect what is still in your backpack, separate sale stock from resources reserved for upgrades, and choose a clear objective for the trip. This guide turns the return to Tresna into a practical departure checklist.

sections.heading: What a death takes
paragraphs: Easy, Normal, and Hard halve the quality of every relic still in the backpack. Expert loses those relics outright. Hardcore, added when version 1.0 left Early Access on September 2, 2026, can end the save and start you over. Difficulty names alone do not tell you which risks apply; read the current mode description. Pick the difficulty by how much of the bag you are willing to lose, not by a damage fantasy the settings do not describe.

Do not assume all difficulty settings protect the same progress. Read the current death description and identify which carried items you would regret losing before choosing the next destination. An item reserved for a near-term upgrade deserves a different decision from a replaceable relic collected for a routine sale. Sort these categories in Tresna, where you can consider the recipe or vendor screen without an encounter demanding your attention. This preparation is especially useful after a long session, when the original reason for carrying an item is easy to forget.

sections.heading: The town order that keeps the bag
paragraphs: Pendant out when the relics are the prize. Sleep in Tresna if the run has left you sloppy. Put the relics on the displays and take the sale. Then buy the potion from Eris at the Witch Hut, or put the coins into a shop level or a vendor unlock. A weapon meter you have not learned is a worse spend than a heal you will use on the next elite. The meter can wait. The bag cannot.

Do not walk back into Kalina with the coins unspent and the bag full. That is the position every death penalty is written to punish. Hotfix 1 did not remove it. The September 10 notes fixed a Kalina hole that could dump you out of the map and waste the run, a Barrier Blessing that failed to restore shield charges on a retry, and legendary chest rewards that failed to appear after a miniboss. Those are reasons to be on the hotfix. They are not a new rule that says the bag is safe.

Before departing, give the trip one purpose: reach a named objective, bring back a needed resource or learn an unfamiliar fight. A full backpack from the previous trip can obscure that purpose. Inspect it slot by slot and decide what still needs to travel. If the intended task is practice, avoid taking a valuable unresolved haul merely because it remains in the bag. If the task is resource collection, leave usable space and identify what you would replace first if a more relevant item appears.
bullets: Buy the potion from Eris
Sell before you upgrade
When to extract

sections.heading: What to write down after the sale
paragraphs: Record the item name, asking price and customer reaction before changing the price. Keep the sale context identifiable: the shop setup, active bonuses and whether a transaction actually completed. A price that was offered is not necessarily a price that sold. At the next session, compare like with like rather than applying one remembered successful price to a different relic or condition.

A useful departure plan includes a stopping condition. Decide what result would make the trip worthwhile and what warning would make you return earlier. The condition can be simple: acquire the material for the next recipe, finish the journal objective, or observe an unfamiliar encounter without adding another expensive experiment. Avoid basing that condition on someone else’s completion percentage. Their unlocked routes, difficulty and equipment may differ from yours. A plan tied to the active save helps you recognize progress even when the trip does not produce a rare drop.

sections.heading: A door you can open
paragraphs: Update to Hotfix 1 or newer. For repeated PC crashes, use a short, controlled API comparison before risking another valuable run. Then look at the bag. If losing half its quality would annoy you, leave. If you are on Expert and losing the relics outright would end the evening, leave. If you are on Hardcore, treat the door as a separate campaign and do not practice the route on the save you care about.

After the next return, compare the plan with the outcome. Which items reached town, which were used, and which were carried without contributing to the objective? Use those answers to prepare the following trip. If the bag repeatedly fills with resources you do not need, change the collection priority rather than buying equipment to solve a storage problem. If you return with the intended materials but cannot afford the purchase, examine the selling decision and the remaining cost. If ordinary fights consume the resources you reserved for the objective, choose a shorter practice route first. Keep these observations attached to the relevant region and difficulty. The aim is a departure inventory whose purpose is clear enough that you can make a replacement or return decision quickly, before another door adds pressure.

moonlighter-2-gun-is-not-a-class.title: The Moonlighter 2 Gun Is Not a Fifth Class
moonlighter-2-gun-is-not-a-class.description: Moonlighter 2 has four melee classes. The gun rides with them. A best-gun search is not a fifth tier list.
moonlighter-2-gun-is-not-a-class.intro: Short Swords, Large Swords, Spears, and Gauntlets are the four melee classes. Each has a Merchant's starter, an Ultimate, named Early Access aspects, a Boss Rush aspect, and an Endless aspect from version 1.0. The gun is the ranged piece that rides alongside that melee weapon. It is not a fifth class with its own Endless Aspect on the launch list.

sections.heading: What the launch post named, and what it did not
paragraphs: Version 1.0 names four Endless Weapon Aspects: Endless Short Sword, Endless Great Sword, Endless Spear, and Endless Gauntlets. Their specials are described. The short sword's special hits more as the combo rises. The great sword blocks, raises Sharpness, and counterattacks. The spear spends stored spearheads and empowers basic attacks. The gauntlets hit harder while Berserk is active. There is no fifth paragraph for an Endless Gun. A best-gun tier list that pretends otherwise is filling a blank.

That does not mean the gun is useless. It means the published comparison is melee-first. Use the gun for the shot the melee special is bad at. Do not respec the whole class because a search query said best gun. The class is the melee weapon you already understand. The gun is the sidearm. Hotfix 1 fixed gadget shots that failed to poison Senda in phase two, and Sergeant Roberto ignoring a distant shot. If the gun felt like it did nothing in early September, retest those two enemies on the hotfix before you bench it forever.

sections.heading: How to pick the melee, then the gun
paragraphs: Pick the Endless aspect whose special matches the room, not a spreadsheet. A short sword special that scales with combo wants a room you can stay in. A great sword stance wants a hit you are willing to block. A spear wants spearheads already stored. Gauntlets want Berserk already up. The gun comes after that choice. If you are still dying before the special matters, the spend is a potion or a piece of armor in Tresna, not a new class.

A gun and an armor purchase solve different problems. Identify whether the last encounter failed because you could not reach a target, could not recover from a commitment, or took an avoidable hit. A ranged tool is worth evaluating when it changes that decision. Test it over a familiar route before committing a valuable haul to an unfamiliar setup.

Keep equipment decisions separate from unrelated unlocks. A shop expansion changes the shop options described in its upgrade screen; it does not establish a gun’s damage, ammunition economy or compatibility with a perk. When planning a purchase, inspect the weapon itself and compare it with what you already use. Identify the gap you are trying to fill before investing in a new gadget. This prevents a general progression milestone from being treated as proof that a particular loadout is ready.

sections.heading: Compare the gun with your melee plan
paragraphs: Choose a ranged tool by the action it adds to your current melee setup. Does it let you act while repositioning, reach an awkward target or apply an effect that your other equipment can use? Compare the description with what happens in a short encounter. Keep enough ammunition or other required resources for the task you intended to solve. A gun that looks impressive during an easy opening may be less useful if you cannot rely on it when the target moves or the room becomes crowded. Judge the pairing on those conditions rather than a store review score.

paragraphs: Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault released version 1.0 on September 2, 2026, the date Digital Sun and 11 bit studios announced on August 5, 2026. This page tracks what each announcement promised and what the launch-day post confirmed shipped.

paragraphs: September 2, 2026. The game had been in Steam Early Access since November 19, 2025, so 1.0 was a transition out of Early Access rather than a first release. The Steam listing now reads Sep 2, 2026 with no Early Access tag.

version-1-0-update.title: Moonlighter 2 Version 1.0: Features and Progression Changes
version-1-0-update.description: Moonlighter 2 version 1.0: the Infinite Endless Vault threshold rule, Hardcore Mode, the four Endless Weapon Aspects, the Bomb Path, Shop Level 5, and physical editions.
version-1-0-update.intro: Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault left Early Access on September 2, 2026. The launch-day announcement from Digital Sun and 11 bit studios is the only first-party description of what actually shipped, and it is unusually specific in some places while giving no numbers at all in others. This page keeps those apart: the rules 1.0 publishes — the Infinite Endless Vault reset condition, what each Endless Weapon Aspect special does, what Hardcore Mode costs you — and the values it never provides.

sections.heading: What actually changed on September 2
paragraphs: The announcement opens with the line that matters for the store page: Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault is “officially out of Early Access on PC, and console versions are available now”. The Steam listing has followed. The release field reads Sep 2, 2026, the Early Access tag is gone, and the genres are now Action, Adventure and RPG.

Note what that sentence does not do: it asserts that console versions exist without naming a single console. Steam still lists Windows as the only platform, so if you came looking for confirmation of a specific console release, the launch post is not it.
bullets: Early Access ran from November 19, 2025 to September 2, 2026 — roughly nine and a half months.
The main story now has an ending. Version 1.0 adds quests, cutscenes and discoveries that bring Will’s journey in Tresna to its conclusion, and changes the world around you along the way.
A postgame exists past that ending, and it is the headline addition rather than a bonus mode.
Platform listed on Steam: Windows. Console versions are asserted by the developer but not named.

sections.heading: The Infinite Endless Vault has one hard rule
paragraphs: The postgame unlocks after you complete the main story, and it is built as “an endless series of increasingly difficult thresholds”. One sentence defines how it works: “Each one must be completed in a single run, meaning that failing to reach the required amount of gold will reset your progress for that threshold.”

That is worth reading twice, because it inverts a habit the rest of the game teaches. A threshold is a gold target, not a boss room, and it is scored per run. Partial progress does not bank. Come up short — by dying, or by leaving early — and that threshold starts from zero. The usual Moonlighter approach of chipping away at a dungeon across several trips does not transfer here.

Rewards scale with how far you push, and the announcement names four categories that unlock along the way: equipment, shop upgrades, decorations and cosmetics. It does not say where the ladder ends. The post poses the question “Can you discover how far the Endless Vault truly goes?” rather than answering it.
bullets: Unlock condition: complete the main story.
Structure: an endless series of thresholds, each harder than the last.
Fail state: not reaching the required gold in one run resets your progress for that threshold.
Scope: one run per threshold, with no partial progress carried between runs.
Rewards: equipment, shop upgrades, decorations and cosmetics.

note.label: No numbers are published
note.text: The announcement gives no gold value for any threshold, no threshold count and no scaling rule. Any specific gold requirement you see quoted is a player measurement, not an official figure.

sections.heading: The four Endless Weapon Aspects, by what their special actually does
paragraphs: These are aspects rather than new weapon types: each one re-specifies the special attack on a weapon class you already use. The descriptions are concrete about mechanics and silent about damage, which means you can plan a build from them but not compute one.
Three of the four are explicitly risk-forward, framed around the Endless Vault’s own philosophy of risk and reward. The Great Sword is the outlier, and the only one whose special opens defensively.
bullets: Endless Short Sword — the special becomes a swift piercing strike that lands multiple hits, and the number of strikes increases with your combo. It pays for keeping momentum instead of resetting between engagements.
Endless Great Sword — crafted by the Golden Guild. The special puts you into a defensive stance that blocks incoming attacks, increases Sharpness, then follows up with a counterattack.

Endless Spear — the special consumes all stored spearheads and turns your basic attacks into empowered special attacks for a limited time, with bonus damage scaling on the number of spearheads consumed.
Endless Gauntlets — while Berserk is active, your attacks become significantly more powerful. This one amplifies a playstyle rather than adding a new input.

sections.heading: The Bomb Path is a perk path, not a gadget
paragraphs: The Bomb Path joins the existing perk paths. It lets you mark enemies with explosive effects that trigger after they have taken a certain number of attacks; when the bomb goes off, it damages nearby enemies.

The trigger is a hit count rather than a timer, which is why the announcement frames the path as a new way to build your deck instead of a new item to use. Two things it does not publish: how many attacks the trigger needs, and how far the explosion reaches.

sections.heading: Shop Level 5 adds exactly two slots
paragraphs: The shop ceiling moved up one level. Shop Level 5 gives more room to customise the shop, and the announcement names precisely two additions: an additional Bloblet slot, and a new cosmetic placement slot for one more decoration.
No unlock cost or requirement is published for Shop Level 5, and the post does not say what the total Bloblet count becomes at that level.

sections.heading: Hardcore Mode, and a wording change worth knowing about
paragraphs: The launch post describes Hardcore Mode in one line: “Death comes with a much greater cost, as dying means losing your progress and starting the journey again from the very beginning.”

The August 5 announcement described the same feature differently. It called the mode Hardcore Difficulty and said it makes “you lose all your relics upon defeat in the ML1 style”. Losing your relics and restarting the whole journey are not the same penalty, and neither post reconciles the two.

This page does not pick a winner. If you are deciding whether to start a Hardcore file, the safe reading is the harsher one: assume a defeat can cost the run from the beginning until the in-game description tells you otherwise.

note.label: Unresolved between two official posts
note.text: August 5, 2026: lose all relics upon defeat. September 2, 2026: lose your progress and start again from the very beginning. Both are first-party. The second describes the build that actually shipped, which is why it is quoted first here.

sections.heading: Three August items the launch post never mentions again
paragraphs: The pre-launch announcement on August 5 listed content that the launch-day post does not bring up. Absence from one post is not removal, but it does mean these items have no launch-day confirmation, so they belong in their own list rather than mixed in above.
bullets: A craftable Machine Gun gadget.
The Endless Armour set — described in August as forged by the Golden Guild, with increased base critical hit chance and additional critical damage for every Spark perk equipped.

Endless Vault VII, described in August as introducing “a brand-new threshold to conquer”. The launch post discusses the Infinite Endless Vault instead and never uses the number VII, so whether these are one feature under two names is not something either announcement settles.
Two named vendors: K33P3R Level 5, and Spark, called an endgame merchant. The launch post confirms “new vendors” without naming any of them.

sections.heading: Everything else 1.0 lists without describing
paragraphs: The closing section of the announcement is a list rather than a description. It is still worth recording, because it marks where 1.0 content exists even though none of it arrives with specifics.
bullets: New vendors.
New Endless Vault cosmetics.
New Codex pages covering enemies, characters, perks and furniture.
Additional quests and cutscenes.
Unspecified improvements.

sections.heading: Physical editions arrive November 13, 2026
paragraphs: Digital Sun and 11 bit studios are partnering with Silver Lining Interactive on physical editions releasing on 13 November 2026, more than two months after the digital launch. Two versions are announced: a standard boxed copy, and a Collector’s Edition.
The Collector’s Edition contents are itemised: art cards, patches, a poster, stickers, a metal coin, and a digital artbook. No price, no platform list and no retailer is given for either edition.

sections.heading: What 1.0 still does not answer
paragraphs: The announcement is a feature list, not a patch note. There is no version string, no build size, and no changelog of balance changes carried over from the last Early Access build. Every new system arrives without numbers attached.
bullets: No gold thresholds, threshold count or scaling rule for the Infinite Endless Vault.
No damage, Sharpness or critical values for any Endless Weapon Aspect.
No hit-count trigger or blast radius for the Bomb Path.
No Shop Level 5 unlock cost, and no final Bloblet total.
No save-transfer or wipe rule for Early Access files — the launch post does not mention saves at all.
No console platform names, despite the post confirming console versions are out.

sections.heading: Shop Level 5 Guide: New Slots Explained
paragraphs: Shop Level 5 raises the shop ceiling in Moonlighter 2 version 1.0. The launch announcement names exactly two additions: an additional Bloblet slot and a new cosmetic placement slot.

sections.heading: What Shop Level 5 adds
paragraphs: The version 1.0 announcement says Shop Level 5 gives more room to customise the shop. Its two named additions are one additional Bloblet slot and one new cosmetic placement slot for another decoration.
bullets: Additional Bloblet slot.
New cosmetic placement slot.
No published unlock cost or requirement in the announcement.

sections.heading: Why this matters to a shop build
paragraphs: The two slots improve shop capacity and presentation, but no official price multiplier, customer formula or decoration bonus is attached to them. Keep “more room” separate from a claim that Level 5 automatically creates more gold.

sections.heading: How to test the upgrade
paragraphs: Record the shop level before and after the upgrade, the number of active Bloblets, the available cosmetic positions and the same item’s customer reaction. Keep the item, price and shop state constant if you want to measure a change rather than a coincidence.

sections.heading: Endless Weapon Aspects Guide
paragraphs: Version 1.0 adds four named Endless Weapon Aspects to Moonlighter 2: Endless Short Sword, Endless Great Sword, Endless Spear and Endless Gauntlets. The official descriptions explain their specials but do not publish their damage values.

sections.heading: Endless Short Sword
paragraphs: Its special becomes a swift piercing strike that lands multiple hits. The number of strikes increases with your combo, so the aspect rewards maintaining momentum between encounters.

sections.heading: Endless Great Sword
paragraphs: The Great Sword aspect is a Golden Guild craft. Its special enters a defensive stance that blocks attacks, increases Sharpness, and then counterattacks. It is the most explicitly defensive description among the four.

sections.heading: Endless Spear
paragraphs: The Spear aspect consumes all stored spearheads. Basic attacks become empowered special attacks for a limited time, with the bonus described as scaling with the number of spearheads consumed.

sections.heading: Endless Gauntlets
paragraphs: The Gauntlets aspect makes attacks significantly more powerful while Berserk is active. It amplifies a state-based build instead of adding a separate published input.

sections.heading: Numbers still need an in-game test
paragraphs: The launch announcement gives no damage, Sharpness, duration, strike-count maximum or acquisition table for the four aspects. Use the description to choose a playstyle, then record a versioned test before calling one the best.

sections.heading: Bomb Path Guide: How the Perk Works
paragraphs: The Bomb Path is a new perk path in Moonlighter 2 version 1.0. It marks enemies with explosive effects that trigger after they take a certain number of attacks and damage nearby enemies when the bomb goes off.

sections.heading: Bomb Path is a perk path
paragraphs: It is not described as a standalone bomb gadget. The launch announcement places it alongside existing perk paths and frames it as a new way to build your deck.

sections.heading: The confirmed trigger loop
paragraphs: Mark an enemy, land the required number of attacks, and let the explosive effect trigger. The resulting blast damages nearby enemies. The exact hit count and blast radius are not published, so do not quote a fixed number without a retail-build test.

sections.heading: How to test the path
paragraphs: Use one enemy group with a stable position. Count attacks from the mark to the detonation, note whether misses or environmental hits count, and record the number of nearby enemies affected. Repeat on the same build before comparing the path with another perk.

moonlighter-2-hotfix-1.title: Moonlighter 2 Hotfix 1: Progression and Stability Fixes
moonlighter-2-hotfix-1.description: Moonlighter 2 version 1.0 Hotfix 1 adds a DirectX 11 / DirectX 12 switch and fixes Kalina map-out bugs, Hazy Jane input loss, the Scarabastion boss invincibility and more.
moonlighter-2-hotfix-1.intro: Eight days after the September 2, 2026 version 1.0 release, Digital Sun shipped Hotfix 1 on September 10. The headline change is a DirectX 11 / DirectX 12 selection option, which the developers tie directly to the crash reports from launch week. The rest of the notes name specific quests, NPCs, enemies, weapons and dungeons that were broken — this page records exactly what the official notes say and what they do not.

sections.heading: The DirectX switch is the stability fix
paragraphs: The notes state that many of the crashes and performance issues players hit may be related to the graphics API, and recommend switching between DirectX 11 and DirectX 12 to see which runs best on your system. If you are crashing on the 1.0 build, this is the first setting to try before anything else.

The developers also say the patch addresses "most of the concerns raised by the community during the 1.0 release" and that further balancing work will be assessed after the console port of these fixes ships.

sections.heading: Progression and quest fixes
bullets: The Weapon Mastery quest marker pointed to the wrong location; fixed.
A crash could occur right after completing a certain main quest; fixed.
Talking to Hazy Jane in later stages could cause a loss of player input; fixed.
The game could freeze on the loading screen when returning to Tresna during the tutorial; fixed.
Babyl sometimes became duplicated, which could make Spark almost impossible to reach if Babyl had not been unlocked yet; fixed.

sections.heading: Enemy behavior fixes
bullets: Senda no longer ignores poison damage from gadget shots during his second phase.
Sergeant Roberto now reacts when shot from a distance.
The CH4 Turret no longer gets stuck in its shooting animation after being tased.
Tased Electric Slimes no longer deal electric field damage.

sections.heading: Weapons, armor and dungeon fixes
bullets: A specific Wound + Ignite perk combination caused a crash; fixed.
Spearhead projectiles froze in midair when reaching Will; fixed.
The second greatsword’s sharpness drain was not working as intended; fixed.
The Vow weapon’s description did not match its actual behavior; fixed.
Equipping the Scarabastion could make players invincible during boss fights; fixed.
A spot in the Kalina dungeon let players fall out of the map with no way to recover the run; fixed.
Will could get stuck behind an obstacle in the Gallery area; fixed.
Barrier Blessing shield charges were not restored when retrying a dungeon; fixed.
Certain rewards did not appear in legendary chests dropped after defeating a miniboss; fixed.
Dungeon music did not restart after the Bloblet room if you left before the track ended; fixed.
The Shared Secret relic description contained placeholder text, debug text and a misspelling; fixed in English and Portuguese.

sections.heading: What the patch does not change
paragraphs: The listed fixes do not provide a replacement weapon damage table. Their absence cannot confirm that every older community statistic remains accurate on a later build. Use the notes to identify the named corrections and check the current item description before relying on an old comparison.

note.label: Verification boundary
note.text: Everything on this page is quoted from the official Hotfix 1 announcement on the Steam news hub for App 2350790, read September 16, 2026. The notes do not publish repro steps or affected-save details, so this page does not invent them.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
bullets: Aeolia is a named area with an Ultimate Challenge achievement.
Hotfix 1 named Kalina (fall out of map) and the Gallery (stuck behind an obstacle), not Aeolia specifically.

sections.heading: What to do
paragraphs: If your run dies to a geometry bug, treat it as a known risk in this dungeon family until a patch names Aeolia. Switch DirectX 11/12 if the issue is a crash rather than a trap.

sections.heading: Screen Flash and Hit Effects
paragraphs: Some players report difficulty with bright hit effects. That feedback is a reason to inspect the available visual settings before committing to a long session, rather than proof of a confirmed developer response or a feature added by Hotfix 1.

sections.heading: What you can do now
paragraphs: Turn effect intensity and screen shake down in the options before you write the game off. If those sliders do not touch the flash you mean, they do not. Hotfix 1's notes are about DirectX, bosses, and input loss, not a photosensitivity preset.

If visual effects cause discomfort, stop the session. The presence of intensity or shake controls does not guarantee that they reduce a particular flash. Describe the specific effect and current platform when asking official support about available settings.

sections.heading: Check the fix on the affected save
paragraphs: A patch note describes the case the developer changed, not every possible cause of the same visible symptom. When checking a progression fix, return to the affected transition with the same quest state if you can do so safely. Confirm that the journal advances and that the destination loads. Do not immediately change equipment, graphics settings and save files together, because a successful result would no longer identify which change mattered. Keep a backup before experimenting with file changes.

For an issue that remains after updating, include the platform and build in the report. Console patches may arrive on a different schedule from a PC update, so verify the version displayed on that device rather than assuming the date on a Steam announcement applies everywhere. Describe the exact action immediately before the problem. A short reproduction sequence is more useful than a general claim that the entire region is broken. Avoid promising that a hotfix will recover every previously damaged save; only the developer can establish that scope.

sections.heading: Aeolia Bugs: Why Runs Get Wasted
paragraphs: If a room prevents progress after updating, note the region, room layout and visible blocker. Record whether an enemy is still present and whether normal movement or attacks respond. Report the reproduction through official support; avoid deleting a working save to test an undocumented workaround.

save-transfer-progress-guide.title: Moonlighter 2 Save Transfer, Cloud Sync and Recovery
save-transfer-progress-guide.description: Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault save transfer guide: what happened at the 1.0 transition, what Steam Cloud covers, and why no official wipe or migration rule was ever published.
save-transfer-progress-guide.intro: Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault ran in Early Access from November 19, 2025 and released version 1.0 on September 2, 2026. Steam lists Steam Cloud, but the launch-day announcement does not mention saves at any point, so there is still no first-party statement about whether an Early Access file carries into 1.0.

sections.heading: Short answer: no official save rule was ever published
paragraphs: The version 1.0 transition has already happened. Digital Sun and 11 bit studios published a long launch-day announcement describing the story conclusion, the postgame, new weapons, a new perk path, a new shop level and a Hardcore mode — and not one line about save files, migration, or a wipe.
That silence is the whole answer to this question. There is no official rule to quote, in either direction.

note.label: Current answer
note.text: No first-party source says Early Access progress is preserved, and none says it is wiped. If your own file loaded normally after updating, that is a personal observation about your save, not a published policy.

sections.heading: What Steam Cloud confirms
paragraphs: The Steam listing includes Steam Cloud. That confirms the feature is offered, but it does not publish a save-slot count, a conflict-resolution rule, or a guarantee that any particular update preserves every field.
bullets: Steam Cloud is listed.
Cross-platform save support is not confirmed by that label.
A migration rule between versions is not confirmed by that label.
The listing does not define how save conflicts or progress variants are handled.

sections.heading: Why this still matters after 1.0
paragraphs: Two groups of players still need this page. The first is anyone who has not launched the game since before September 2, 2026 and wants to know what happens to an old file on first load. The second is anyone playing now, because 1.0 is a starting point for patches rather than the end of updates, and the same absence of a published policy applies to those.

A third case is specific to the launch build: Hardcore Mode carries its own progress penalty by design. That is a game rule, not a save-transfer rule, and the two should not be confused when reading community reports.

sections.heading: Low-risk preparation for any update
paragraphs: The safest preparation is reversible and does not depend on an invented file path or migration command. Keep an offline backup of important save data before a major update, and keep that backup separate from any copy created afterwards.
bullets: Record the current game version and the progress you want to check after the update.
Copy your save data somewhere outside the game folder before applying a large patch.
Do not overwrite the pre-update backup until you have confirmed the post-update result yourself.
Treat Steam Cloud as a listed feature, not as proof of cross-version preservation.
Keep any official version note that does discuss saves, since that would be the first real rule published.

sections.heading: How to read the Steam Cloud status safely
paragraphs: For this question, the useful confirmed fact is simply that Steam Cloud appears in the Steam feature listing. Use that to confirm the feature remains advertised, but do not turn it into a claim about cross-platform saves, a guaranteed restore, or a wipe decision. Those are separate questions that need explicit wording from the developer or a version note.

sections.heading: What to watch for next
paragraphs: A real update on this would come from Digital Sun or 11 bit studios in a developer announcement, patch note, or version note. Look for direct wording about save migration, wipe behavior, compatibility with existing progress, and any required player action. Until those terms are published, this page stays a preparation guide rather than a promise.

sections.heading: Autosave: You Cannot Sleep Mid-Run
paragraphs: Steam Cloud and in-game saving solve different problems. Cloud synchronization transfers available save data; it does not determine when an expedition is written to the local save. Before a long trip, inspect the game’s current save feedback and use its normal save or exit sequence. Do not interrupt the process merely because the Steam library lists Cloud support.

sections.heading: What the loop actually saves
paragraphs: After an expedition, finish the hub actions you intended to preserve and look for the normal save indication before closing. On the next launch, confirm the intended slot and progression. If the result is unexpected, preserve the copies you have and investigate the synchronization state before starting another session that could overwrite them.
Steam Cloud is on the listing. It syncs a file that exists. It does not add a mid-floor rest. See save transfer for the 1.0 migration silence, and the shop for the counter you still run yourself.
bullets: Extraction
The register

sections.heading: Keep recovery separate from migration
paragraphs: Before migrating a save, decide which copy represents the progress you want to keep. Compare the displayed character or slot, quest state and most recent successful session. A newer timestamp alone may reflect a failed session or a cloud operation, rather than the furthest campaign progress. Close the game before copying local data. Preserve an untouched backup outside the active save location so a later sync cannot silently replace the only recovery copy.

After moving to another installation, open the intended slot and check the parts of progress that matter to you: the current quest, the town services you unlocked and the equipment you expected to own. If the wrong state appears, stop playing before generating more writes. Do not switch repeatedly between two devices while trying to decide which copy is correct. Cloud support confirms a synchronization feature, not a guarantee that two divergent histories will merge. For uncertain cases, collect the platform and slot information and request support before overwriting files.

shop-guide.title: Moonlighter 2 Shop Guide: Stock, Selling and Reinvestment
shop-guide.description: A source-tracked Moonlighter 2 shop guide covering player-set prices, customers, decorations, perks, and village investment.
shop-guide.intro: The shop is not a separate menu from the adventure. Steam describes a merchant who returns from dangerous dimensions, arranges loot, reads customers, sets prices, uses special events, and invests in the village.

sections.heading: Price with customer feedback in mind
paragraphs: The Steam description explicitly says the player sets their own price and reads customers to score the perfect deal. That supports a test-driven price log, but not a single price formula until the released build can be measured.
bullets: Record the displayed reaction instead of translating it into an assumed percentage.
Keep special-event rows separate because Steam says events can build sales momentum.
Compare results after shop decoration and perk changes rather than mixing all conditions together.

sections.heading: Shop and village progression
paragraphs: Steam says shop decorations and perks can improve sales momentum, while village investment unlocks better weapons, armor, and upgrades. The practical guide order is therefore run, sell, reinvest, then test the next run under the new condition.

note.label: Verified boundary
note.text: The categories are official. Exact decoration effects, perk names, unlock costs, and the best upgrade order still require hands-on data.

sections.heading: Shop Level 5 is the version 1.0 ceiling
paragraphs: Version 1.0 raised the shop ceiling by one level. The launch announcement names exactly two things Shop Level 5 adds: an additional Bloblet slot, and a new cosmetic placement slot for one more decoration.
It does not publish the unlock requirement, the unlock cost, or the total Bloblet count at that level, so treat the level as confirmed and the numbers around it as untested.

sections.heading: The order
paragraphs: Pendant out when the relics are the prize. Sleep in Tresna if the run left you sloppy. Put the relics on the displays. Take the sale. Then buy the potion from Eris, or a piece of armor that stays when you die. A weapon meter you have not learned is a worse spend than a heal you will use on the next elite.

Check the current difficulty before assuming what a failed expedition will preserve. Prepare sale stock and recipe reserves separately, then choose the next purchase from the failure that actually limited the last trip. A repeated combat mistake may call for practice rather than another shop decoration. A comfortable route with poor returns may call for better stock and pricing decisions. Use the resources shown in the current save instead of treating a generic priority list as a compulsory build.

sections.heading: Record a sale before changing the setup
paragraphs: Write the number that sold and the number that offended. Steam did not print that table. A player stuck on the first boss still recommended the game in a shorter file. They would have had a calmer door if the bag had been empty. Sleep is part of the loop, a useful part of the shop loop.
bullets: Eris, after the sale
Why the bag is the wager
Crash before you can sell? Switch API.

sections.heading: Then stop
paragraphs: Before opening the shop, choose the items intended for sale and keep materials for the next planned recipe separate. Read the displayed price information and watch the customer response before making another change. If you alter several prices and activate a shop effect together, it becomes difficult to tell which choice affected the result. A small consistent comparison helps you decide whether the next session should focus on stock, prices or a particular upgrade.

sections.heading: Shop Level 5 Is a Slot, Not a Build
paragraphs: The September 2, 2026 launch post names Shop Level 5 as one more Bloblet slot and one more cosmetic placement slot. That is a shop slot. It is not a defense number and not an Endless Weapon Aspect.

sections.heading: What the slot is
paragraphs: One more Bloblet. One more place to put a cosmetic. The post confirmed the slots. It did not print a damage table for the decoration. Armor is a separate town purchase. The gun rides beside four melee classes. The Endless aspects are Short Sword, Great Sword, Spear, and Gauntlets. None of those is a floor tile.

Buy the slot after you can survive a death with an empty enough bag. Sell first. Town purchases stay. Backpack relics may not. A cosmetic funded by carrying relics back into Kalina is a cosmetic you may not get to place.

sections.heading: Compare capacity with the current shop plan
bullets: The two additions, named
Armor is the other purchase
Fund the slot after the sale

sections.heading: When to buy it
paragraphs: Choose an expansion when you can explain how you will use its added capacity. Inspect the upgrade cost and the equipment or supplies you still need for your next trip. If the new slot would sit unused because you have no suitable companion or decoration, a different purchase may solve a more immediate problem. If you already have a clear shop setup waiting for the space, compare the expected convenience with its cost. This is a planning decision rather than a mandatory order for every save.

sections.heading: Moonlighter 2: Sell the Bag Before You Upgrade
paragraphs: The first sale creates several competing options: supplies, equipment, village services and shop improvements. Inspect what is available and choose the one that removes the clearest immediate obstacle. Keep a reserve if a recipe or service you intend to use still has an unmet cost. There is no need to buy one item from every category before returning to a familiar route. A focused purchase is easier to evaluate because you know what it was meant to improve.

sections.heading: A return to town, in order
paragraphs: Extract with the pendant if the bag is the prize. Sleep is the hub save. You cannot sleep mid-run. Put relics on the displays, read the customer, and take the sale before you open a weapon menu.

Eris at the Witch Hut is the first vendor players upgrade: potions, health, and dungeon perk unlocks. Ms. Scratch raises the shop level. K33P3R adds merchant bonuses. The Countess sells showcases that raise a whole rarity. Those are safe spends. A new sword is not, until the meter on the current one is boring.

sections.heading: Sell the Bag, Then Sleep in Tresna
paragraphs: Before leaving town again, check the intended sale items, reserve materials and the current save state. Finish the actions needed for the next objective rather than assuming returning to the hub alone completed every transaction. Confirm your equipment and departure inventory before opening another run.

dungeon-guide.title: Moonlighter 2 Dungeon Guide: Routes, Combat and Run Decisions
dungeon-guide.description: A Moonlighter 2 dungeon guide grounded in the Steam description: route planning, relic collection, backpack space, and escalating rewards.
dungeon-guide.intro: Steam describes dangerous dungeons and vibrant dimensions full of loot and enemies. It also says deeper exploration brings greater rewards, which makes route planning and extraction decisions central to the guide.

sections.heading: The three dimensions
paragraphs: Moonlighter 2 has three dimensions, each with an easier first floor and a harder second floor, and each running its own relic curse. Floors unlock through Tresna story quests rather than levels.
bullets: Kalina — desert dimension; Burn and Armor curse; bosses The Herald and Thalaam.
The Gallery — museum-machine dimension; Shock and Overcharge curse; bosses The Curator and Tyke.
Aeolia — windy magic isles; Petrify and Absorb curse; bosses Senda and Monte.

sections.heading: Plan the run around extraction
paragraphs: The published game description advises players to plot a clever route, arrange loot carefully, and remember that deeper runs bring greater rewards. This gives us a confirmed decision pattern: what to carry, how far to push, and when to return matter as much as clearing enemies.
bullets: Start with a route that leaves room for the loot you expect to collect.
The pendant teleports you home at any time with everything in the bag; there is no penalty beyond skipped loot.
Record the depth, loot category, and outcome for every repeatable run.

sections.heading: Endless Vault context
paragraphs: The Endless Vault is described as an ancient artifact whose trials test merchants and raise the stakes for rewards and town upgrades. Its exact rooms, encounters, and boss behavior are not published in the Steam description.

sections.heading: The Infinite Endless Vault changes how you plan a run
paragraphs: Version 1.0 added a postgame that unlocks after the main story, and it is the one place where the extraction decision has a published rule. The launch announcement describes an endless series of increasingly difficult thresholds and states that each one must be completed in a single run — failing to reach the required amount of gold resets your progress for that threshold.

That makes gold, not depth, the scoring metric there, and it removes the option of banking partial progress across trips. No gold target, threshold count or scaling rule has been published, so the only honest planning advice is to treat every threshold attempt as a single closed run.

sections.heading: Tomo’s Radar: Every Node Type and Which Branch to Take
paragraphs: Tomo’s Radar turns each floor into a branching map, and you choose one branch at every step. The run is decided here, not in the fights — a route that skips the perk room and ends on an elite is a route you planned badly.

sections.heading: The node types
paragraphs: Every floor in all three dimensions uses the same node vocabulary. Learn it once and the routing transfers.
bullets: **Chest** — a few Common relics plus a choice between two higher-rarity ones
**Event** — a situational room; take it when the bag is light
**Potion** — healing stock, which is the cheapest insurance in the game
**Blacksmith** — in-run weapon work
**Recipe** — unlocks, including gadget recipes
**Ice or Thunder perk rooms** — combat pedestals that hand out run perks
**Elite**, **Miniboss**, **Boss** — the fights that gate materials and quests

sections.heading: Node colour is the quality dial
paragraphs: Chests appear after chest nodes, minibosses and bosses, and **the node colour on the radar sets the relic quality** inside. A longer branch through richer nodes is worth more than a short branch to the boss.
That is the whole routing decision in one sentence: you are not choosing a path to the exit, you are choosing how much the bag is worth when you get there.

sections.heading: A branch order that works
paragraphs: **Perk room first.** A perk you take on node two works for the whole floor; the same perk taken before the boss works for one fight. The perk path guide covers which to stack.
**Potions before elites.** Elites and minibosses never rupture, so you cannot clear a bad fight with a backpack launch. Healing is how you survive them.
**Chests while the bag has room.** A high-rarity chest you cannot carry is worse than a Common one you can — and the curse rules mean "room" is not just empty slots.

**Miniboss for materials.** Each floor’s two minibosses drop the material for that dimension’s early weapon upgrades, and Nou and Anacard at the Silent Exchange will swap surplus miniboss materials for boss materials.

sections.heading: When to stop routing and leave
paragraphs: The pendant teleports you home at any time with everything in the bag, and there is no penalty beyond the loot you skipped. "Back to Tresna" relic effects also trigger on the way out.

Because floors unlock through Tresna story quests rather than levels, there is no XP to grind — extract and bank freely. The only thing a longer run buys is relics and materials, and the only thing it risks is the bag you already filled.

Dungeon guide
What death costs

sections.heading: Perk Paths: Stack One Element, Not Three
paragraphs: Combat pedestals hand out run perks, and the single biggest damage decision in a run is whether you stack one element or collect a souvenir from each. Stacking wins, and it is not close.

sections.heading: Stack one path
paragraphs: Perk rooms on Tomo’s Radar come in **Ice** and **Thunder** flavours, and pedestals inside hand out the run perks. Taking all Thunder, or all Ignite, beats mixing — the stacked path compounds, the mixed one gives you three effects that never reach the threshold where they matter.
Pick the element on the first perk room you enter and then route toward more of it. A run where you took one of everything is a run where nothing procced.

sections.heading: One on the gun, one on the weapon
paragraphs: The usual split is **one perk on the gun and one on the melee weapon**. That covers both ranges without breaking the stack, because both are feeding the same element.

This is also why weapon class matters here: a Short Sword still needs its three-hit finisher to land, and Gauntlets are a burst tool for a short recovery window. A perk that triggers on hit count behaves very differently on each.

sections.heading: Perks are not boons, and neither is an Aspect
paragraphs: Three separate systems share the word "upgrade" and they do not stack into one plan:

Run **perks** come from combat pedestals inside a floor and last for that run. **Boons** are limited to two per run, and a third offer replaces one rather than adding to it. **Endless Weapon Aspects** are a version 1.0 weapon system and have nothing to do with either.
bullets: Only two boons per run
Endless Weapon Aspects
Bomb Path

sections.heading: Route for the perk, then for the chest
paragraphs: A perk room taken early works for the entire floor. A perk room taken before the boss works for one fight. If the radar offers a perk branch and a chest branch at node two, the perk is almost always the better pick — the chest at the end of a stacked run is worth more anyway.

If the next node is an elite or a miniboss, take the perk that answers that room rather than the one that fits your fantasy build. Elites do not rupture, so damage you cannot apply is damage you do not have.

sections.heading: Rupture: The Backpack Launch and What It Does Not Work On
paragraphs: Rupture is the most satisfying mechanic in the game and the most commonly misread. An enemy at half health turns purple, and the backpack launches it into a wall, into another enemy, or off the edge. It also never, ever works on the fights where you most want it.

sections.heading: How a rupture happens
paragraphs: Bring a normal enemy to **half health** and it turns purple. That purple state is the window: the backpack launch sends it flying into walls, into other enemies, or off a ledge entirely.

The launch is crowd control as much as damage. A purple enemy thrown into a group is how you reset a room that was closing in on you, and an edge is a free kill regardless of what health the target had left.

sections.heading: What never ruptures
paragraphs: **Elites and minibosses never rupture. Bosses never rupture.** This is the rule people learn the hard way, usually in a boss doorway with a full bag.
If a fight is an elite, a miniboss or a boss, the backpack is not a weapon — it is just your inventory. Everything in that fight has to be solved with the weapon meter, the perk stack and your dodge.

note.label: Rule of thumb
note.text: If it has a name on the radar, it does not rupture.

sections.heading: Purple is the signal to change targets
paragraphs: In a mixed room, a purple enemy is worth more than a full-health one, because the launch is faster than finishing it normally and it damages whatever it lands on. Switch targets when something turns purple rather than finishing the swing you started.
Against groups beside a ledge, this flips the whole fight: you are no longer killing six enemies, you are rupturing three and throwing them at the other three.

sections.heading: Why it matters for the bag
paragraphs: The backpack is both your launcher and your loot, which is the joke the system is built on. You cannot free up space mid-fight by rupturing, and the space you walked in with is the space you fight with.
That is also why a full bag in front of a boss door is a decision, not an accident — the pendant is still right there.

sections.heading: Healing: Why the First Game's Dodge Window Is Gone
paragraphs: The complaint that shows up next to the praise is healing. You cannot cancel an attack into a dodge the way Moonlighter 1 allowed. A swing you committed to is a hit you eat.

sections.heading: What to change
paragraphs: Stop swinging when an elite winds up. The desert elites with the red telegraph are the lesson. The dodge is before the swing, not during it.
Buy healing at the shop before you buy a damage toy you cannot survive long enough to use. Shop Level 5 does not refund a death.
If the screen flash on hits is the actual problem, that is a separate accessibility complaint players have filed. It is not a healing potion.

sections.heading: Elite Telegraphs in the Desert Region
paragraphs: The desert platforms show the tell: a red body, a wind-up, a bridge you should not be standing on. That enemy is why healing feels scarce.

sections.heading: The tell
paragraphs: If the elite is glowing, you are late to move and early to extract. Kill the small ones first only if they body-block the dodge.
A full bag on that bridge is a failed run even if you win the fight. Extraction is the win condition. The kill is optional.
